summary: Expose write-worker admission backlog and abandoned callback starts

replay.detail: No claim, projection or replay changes.

schema.detail: Queue timestamps and requester liveness are process-local; storage schema and digests are unchanged.

rules.detail: Writer admission, dependent permit sharing and detached mutation completion are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: The existing OTel pipeline exports st.write_workers.queue.depth, st.write_workers.queue.mean_age (seconds, maximum per-store mean queued age), st.write_workers.queue.busy_age (seconds, maximum per-store busy-period age: a conservative upper bound on oldest queued age, not exact), st.write_workers.queue.wait (seconds, bounded normalized route origin), and st.write_workers.abandoned_callback_starts (outcome=ran, per callback poll rather than unique request). Atomic aggregates replace the proposed locked oldest-age metric. Mean sampling checks depth before and after the timestamp sum, retries three times and emits zero if unstable or empty; mean age remains approximate and can hide old outliers. Alerts use busy_age instead: a continuously nonempty queue never resets, and overlapping empty transitions may retain an earlier start, so false positives are possible. Busy start is atomically published on 0-to-1 depth transitions; clearing on 1-to-0 rechecks depth and restores an earlier start if enqueue raced the clear. Empty observations emit zero. Observable gauges include admission and blocking-pool waits until callback start; explicit admission leaves the queue at grant. Dropped request waiters are observed without skipping work.

downtime.detail: No additional downtime beyond the normal binary restart.

manual.detail: Existing OTel exporter configuration applies. No additional setup is required.

recovery.detail: Binary swap-back requires no data migration.
